headline: September US producer prices jumped 1.3 percent on the month, the hottest print in years, and the 10 year Treasury yield still fell about 10 basis points to 5.089 percent as money left debt funded AI names for bonds and defensives, pushing CoreWeave credit default swaps to distress levels while Apple's market value went back above 5 trillion dollars and gold rose 1.54 percent.

summary.us: Headline producer prices rose 1.3 percent on the month and 6.3 percent on the year with core up 0.7 percent against a 0.3 percent forecast, yet the 10 year yield fell to 5.089 percent because investors bought safety as the AI credit trade cracked, with CoreWeave credit default swaps at distress levels and its 2032 bonds near a 15 percent yield. The Dow rose about 1.1 percent and the S&P 500 added 0.33 percent to 7,744.06 while the Nasdaq Composite was flat at 26,713.03, as money rotated into software and defensives, ServiceNow gained 6.14 percent, Intuit 6.36 percent on its Sequence acquisition and Apple held near a record after Tuesday's all time closing high.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 closed 1.66 percent higher at 22,997.35 and Bank Nifty gained 0.89 percent to 55,810.50, led by IT after Wipro's results lifted the Nifty IT index about 2 percent, and by Reliance, which rose 3.44 percent after Jio Platforms set a 1,065 to 1,119 rupee band for its 30,213 crore rupee IPO opening Oct 21. The rupee closed near 95.05 per dollar for a fifth straight gain on the RBI foreign exchange measures announced Oct 10, September wholesale inflation came in at 11.39 percent against a 10.18 percent forecast, and provisional FII and DII cash flow figures conflicted across aggregators this run so no number is quoted.
summary.global: Asia absorbed the AI selloff on Thursday, with the Nikkei 225 down 4.77 percent for a sixth straight fall, the Kospi triggering circuit breakers after dropping as much as 8 percent and the Hang Seng off 1.03 percent to 24,062.72 as its tech gauge lost 2.72 percent, while Europe closed higher with the FTSE 100 up 1.08 percent and the DAX up 0.33 percent. Japan and Korea rebounded Friday morning, the Nikkei up 1.79 percent and the Kospi up 3.31 percent, and TSMC reported record third quarter revenue of about 46.7 billion dollars with 2026 capital spending held at 60 to 64 billion dollars and 2026 to 2028 spending flagged as significantly higher.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on the long end of the Treasury curve, where yields pushed to multi year highs midweek and the 30 year auction cleared at 5.618 percent, the highest since August 2000, before solid demand cooled the move and let the S&P 500 finish 1.15 percent higher and the Nasdaq 0.64 percent higher despite a Thursday air pocket when the Financial Times reported OpenAI annualized revenue about 20 billion dollars below the figure circulated to investors. India spent the week absorbing the RBI's first rate hike since February 2023, a 25 basis point move to 5.50 percent on Oct 7 paired with a hawkish calibrated tightening stance and an FY27 CPI forecast lifted to 5.2 percent, which left the Nifty up only 0.44 percent while Bank Nifty gained 1.48 percent and foreign investors kept selling, including a 12,944 crore rupee outflow on Oct 8. Metals were the cleanest trade, with copper up 3.37 percent on the Centinela strike in Chile and Chinese restocking, and silver and gold adding 1.89 and 1.39 percent as real yields retreated into Friday. Crypto went the other way, bitcoin down 2.58 percent and ether down 7.34 percent on the week, pressured by high oil costs, rate hike expectations and Middle East risk. Next week brings the first real test of earnings season, with JPMorgan and Citigroup on Oct 13 and Bank of America on Oct 14, alongside US September CPI on Oct 14 that the street expects at 3.6 percent on the year, India September CPI, and TSMC results on Oct 15.
